ctor.issue: CURSE / CURSE / NONE map exactly. The canonical energy cost is -1 in C# and 0 in the sim. `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers` returns early on `_base < 0` (CardEnergyCost.cs:100-103), so the game's unplayable card is immune to every cost modifier and keeps reporting -1; the sim runs a base of 0 through the full modifier chain (cards/base.py:222-232). `GetAmountToSpend()` clamps to Math.Max(0, ...) on both sides, so only what is READ diverges. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/ascenders_bane's ctor entry (rule 3). DORMANT: the ported cost readers all filter `> 0` or skip `<= 1` (relics/mummified_hand.py:25, potions.py:168, cards/event_cards.py:328), and events/infested_automaton.py:35 filters pool_card_ids(), which holds no curses or statuses.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: nothing -- the sim passes the literal 1 (doubt.py:42)
CanonicalVars.issue: `new PowerVar<WeakPower>(1m)` (Doubt.cs:20) is a printed var with no `_weak` in `_init_vars`, so `magic_number` returns None where the game prints 1. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed DynamicVar with no `_`-attribute in `_init_vars`, so the sim's printed-number API reports the default and `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card wrongly for the policy. DORMANT for game fidelity (the dealt/applied number is identical), LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnTurnEndInHand.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<WeakPower>(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.Weak.BaseValue, null, this)` (Doubt.cs:32) == `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, WeakPower, 1)`. The NULL applier is reproduced (the sim leaves `applier` at its None default), which matters for anything keyed on who applied the debuff. The explicit `if (powerModel != null && !alreadyHasWeak) powerModel.SkipNextDurationTick = true` (33-36) needs no counterpart: `PowerCmd.Apply` already sets that flag unconditionally for player-side debuffs on the NEW-power path (PowerCmd.cs:144-147), so Doubt's line is redundant with the engine in the fresh case and correctly absent in the already-Weak case. The sim's own `PowerCmd.apply` sets `skip_next_tick` at cmds.py:331-332. BLAST RADIUS, not re-verdicted here per rule 3: the sim's flag sits AFTER the new-vs-stacking if/else, so it also fires on RE-STACKING where C# does not -- already recorded as power_cmd step 20.
